baseline:
B
A standard transformer block consists of a multi-head attention layer followed by a position-wise feed-forward network, which is a type of MLP.

B
An MLP is characterized by having at least one hidden layer of neurons between the input and output layers. The use of non-linear activation functions (like ReLU or sigmoid) is crucial, as they allow the network to learn complex, non-linear patterns in the data.

B
The MLP, also known as the position-wise feed-forward network, processes the output of the attention layer. This output is a set of context-aware embeddings. The MLP applies a non-linear transformation to each embedding individually, allowing the model to process the information gathered by the attention mechanism in a more complex way.

C
The MLP's weights are trained to map specific input patterns (keys) to desired output patterns (values), effectively encoding and storing factual associations learned from the training data.

C
The weights (W) and biases (b) are the parameters of the network that are adjusted during the training process. This process encodes the learned patterns and relationships from the data directly into the numerical values of W and b, which effectively serve as the model's memory.
